provenance.l: Vega 1 — 1,500 kg descent unit (2.4 m sphere), entry at 125 km and ~11 km/s, first parachute at 64 km; entry to touchdown 02:06:10 → 03:02:54 UT (3404 s). Lander mass after the balloon and shell leave, chute release altitude and disc drag are estimates fitted to the 3404 s

Sagdeev et al. 1986 (NASA TM-88516): drogue chute at 64 km, balloon probe detaches at 61 km (t=70 s), balloon parachute at 55 km (t=200 s), balloon fills at 54 km (t=300 s), ballast dropped at 50 km, then it floats at 53-54 km; 3.4 m shell, 21 kg total; drifted 46 h, 11,500 km at ~69 m/s. The lander's own descent is unchanged. The balloon's altitudes are the balloon's own; the scene keys them to the lander's altitude as the nearest drawn instant, and its drift and rise away from the lander are drawn, not sourced
